slsa_requirements.title: Provenance Exists
slsa_requirements.description: The software producer creates provenance documentation that describes how the artifact was built, including the build platform, build process, and top-level inputs. At Level 1, provenance does not need to be authenticated or generated by the build system itself; manual or script-generated provenance is acceptable. The goal is to establish a baseline of provenance availability.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance documentation exists for the artifact. The provenance identifies the build platform, entry point, and top-level source. Consumers can locate and retrieve the provenance for any given artifact.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Generate provenance as part of the build process using any method: manual documentation, build scripts that emit provenance, or CI/CD pipeline metadata. Consider using SLSA provenance generators available for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and other platforms.

slsa_requirements.title: Provenance Format Compliance
slsa_requirements.description: Provenance must follow a documented, consistent format that enables automated processing. SLSA recommends using the in-toto attestation format with the SLSA Provenance predicate type. At Level 1, any consistent format is acceptable, but using the standard format improves interoperability with verification tools and downstream consumers.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance follows a consistent, documented format. The format includes required fields: builder identity, build configuration source, and build inputs. The provenance can be parsed by standard tooling.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use the in-toto attestation framework (https://in-toto.io) with SLSA Provenance v1 predicate type. The provenance should be serialized as a DSSE envelope for later signing at higher levels.

slsa_requirements.title: Source Repository Identified
slsa_requirements.description: The provenance must identify the source repository from which the artifact was built. This establishes the link between a built artifact and its source code, enabling consumers to audit the source, review commit history, and verify that the source matches expectations. At Level 1, the source identity is self-declared.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance includes the source repository URI. The specific revision (commit hash, tag, or branch) used for the build is documented. Consumers can locate the source code from the provenance information.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Capture the full source repository URL and the exact commit SHA used for the build. Include this in the provenance materials or resolvedDependencies section. For Git repositories, use the full commit hash (40 hex characters), not abbreviated hashes.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Process Documentation
slsa_requirements.description: The build process must be documented well enough that another party could reasonably reproduce the build. This includes build commands, environment requirements, build dependencies, and configuration parameters. Documentation does not require the build to be actually reproducible, only that the process is transparent and understandable.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build commands and configuration are documented. Build environment requirements (OS, runtime, tool versions) are specified. A reasonably skilled developer could follow the documentation to perform the build.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Maintain build instructions in the repository (Makefile, build.sh, CI config). Document required build tools and their versions. Include environment variable requirements and configuration options. Consider using containerized builds for environment consistency.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Dependencies Listed
slsa_requirements.description: All direct build dependencies must be listed in the provenance or in a companion SBOM. This includes libraries, tools, base images, and other components consumed during the build. Dependency listing is the foundation for vulnerability analysis, license compliance, and understanding the full supply chain of the artifact.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: A list of direct dependencies is available. Dependencies include version information. The dependency list is associated with the specific build that produced the artifact.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use package manager lock files (package-lock.json, go.sum, Cargo.lock) to capture exact dependency versions. Generate an SBOM as part of the build process. Include lock files in version control. Consider using tools like syft, cdxgen, or spdx-sbom-generator.

slsa_requirements.title: Artifact Uniquely Identifiable
slsa_requirements.description: The built artifact must be uniquely identifiable, typically through a cryptographic digest (hash). This enables consumers to verify that the artifact they received matches the one described in the provenance. Without unique artifact identification, provenance cannot be meaningfully bound to a specific artifact.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: The artifact has a cryptographic digest (SHA-256 or stronger). The provenance references the artifact by its digest. Consumers can compute the digest of the artifact they received and compare it to the provenance.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Compute SHA-256 (or SHA-512) digest of all published artifacts. Include the digest in the provenance subject field. Publish digests alongside artifacts (e.g., SHA256SUMS file). Use content-addressable storage where possible.

slsa_requirements.title: Scripted Build Process
slsa_requirements.description: The build process should be fully scripted rather than relying on manual commands. Scripted builds ensure consistency, reduce human error, and enable automation. While Level 1 allows some manual steps, the core build logic should be captured in build scripts, Makefiles, or CI/CD pipeline definitions that can be version-controlled and audited.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build can be executed by running a defined script or command. Build scripts are version-controlled alongside the source code. Manual intervention is minimized or documented as exceptions.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Define the entire build process in scripts (Makefile, npm scripts, Gradle tasks). Store build definitions in the source repository. Use CI/CD pipeline definitions (GitHub Actions workflows, GitLab CI YAML) as the authoritative build process. Avoid undocumented manual build steps.

slsa_requirements.title: Provenance Retention
slsa_requirements.description: Provenance documents must be retained for a defined period and remain accessible to consumers. Without retention policies, provenance becomes unavailable when consumers need to verify artifacts at a later date, such as during incident response or compliance audits. At Level 1, the retention period and storage mechanism are at the producer's discretion.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: A retention policy exists for provenance documents. Provenance is stored in a durable, accessible location. Historical provenance can be retrieved for previously published artifacts.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Store provenance alongside published artifacts in the package registry. Use transparency logs like Rekor for public provenance. Define a retention period aligned with your software support lifecycle (minimum recommended: product end-of-life + 1 year). Consider regulatory retention requirements (EU CRA: 10 years).

slsa_requirements.title: Hosted Build Platform
slsa_requirements.description: Builds must be executed on a hosted, managed build platform rather than on developer workstations. Hosted build platforms provide a controlled environment with audit logging, access controls, and consistent configuration. This reduces the risk of compromised developer environments injecting malicious code during the build process.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Builds execute on a hosted CI/CD service (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, etc.). Build logs are generated by the platform. The build platform identity is recorded in the provenance.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use managed CI/CD services: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps Pipelines, Google Cloud Build, AWS CodeBuild, or self-hosted equivalents with equivalent security controls. Ensure the build platform generates audit logs and supports identity verification.

slsa_requirements.title: Authenticated Provenance
slsa_requirements.description: Provenance must be digitally signed by the build platform to establish authenticity. The signature must be verifiable by consumers using the build platform's public key or certificate chain. Authenticated provenance ensures that the provenance was generated by the claimed build platform and has not been tampered with after generation.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance is digitally signed using DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope) or equivalent. The signature can be verified against the build platform's public key. The signing identity is traceable to the build platform.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use Sigstore for keyless signing with OIDC identity (recommended for open source). For private builds, use organizational PKI. GitHub Actions: use slsa-github-generator. GitLab CI: use cosign with OIDC. Store signatures alongside provenance or in a transparency log (Rekor).

slsa_requirements.title: Build Platform Generates Provenance
slsa_requirements.description: Provenance must be generated by the build platform itself, not by the build script or the project's own code. This is a critical trust boundary: if the build script generates its own provenance, a compromised build script could forge provenance. The build platform, as a trusted third party, must be the provenance generator.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance is generated by the build platform infrastructure, not by user-controlled build scripts. The provenance generation mechanism is isolated from the build process. The build platform's identity is verifiable in the provenance.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use platform-native provenance generators: slsa-github-generator for GitHub Actions, GitLab's built-in attestation support, Google Cloud Build's provenance feature. Do not rely on build scripts calling tools like in-toto-run, as the build script itself is within the trust boundary of the attacker.

slsa_requirements.title: Version-Controlled Source
slsa_requirements.description: All source code must be stored in a version control system that maintains a complete history of changes. This enables auditing of code changes, identification of when vulnerabilities were introduced, and rollback to known-good states. The VCS must support immutable revision identifiers (e.g., Git commit hashes).
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Source code is managed in a version control system (Git, Mercurial, etc.). Every build references a specific, immutable revision identifier. The complete change history is retained and auditable.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use Git with a hosted platform (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket). Ensure all builds reference specific commit SHAs, not mutable references like branch names. Protect the default branch with branch protection rules. Maintain complete commit history (avoid force-push to main/production branches).

slsa_requirements.title: Build Service Account Isolation
slsa_requirements.description: The build service must use dedicated service accounts with minimal required permissions. Build service credentials should not be shared across projects or reused for non-build purposes. This limits the blast radius of a compromised build and prevents lateral movement between projects through shared credentials.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build service accounts are project-specific or have scoped permissions. Service accounts follow the principle of least privilege. Credentials are not shared across unrelated projects. Access to build service accounts is audited.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use separate service accounts for each project or repository. Grant minimum required permissions using OIDC federation where possible (eliminates long-lived credentials). Regularly rotate service account credentials. Audit service account usage and permissions.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Configuration from External Source
slsa_requirements.description: The build configuration (CI/CD pipeline definition) must be fetched from a version-controlled source at build time. The build platform must identify the configuration source in the provenance. This ensures that the build configuration itself is auditable and that changes to build processes are tracked in version control.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build configuration files are stored in version control. The build platform fetches configuration from the VCS at build time. The provenance records the configuration source and revision.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Store CI/CD pipeline definitions in the source repository (.github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, azure-pipelines.yml). Ensure the build platform uses the configuration from the same commit being built. Avoid out-of-band configuration that is not version-controlled.

slsa_requirements.title: Provenance Non-Falsifiable by Build Tenants
slsa_requirements.description: Build tenants (the users/projects using the build platform) must not be able to forge or tamper with provenance. The provenance generation must be controlled by the build platform infrastructure, outside the control of the tenant's build scripts. This prevents a malicious build script from claiming false build inputs or builder identity.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Tenants cannot directly write to provenance storage. Provenance is generated by platform infrastructure, not tenant code. The platform enforces that provenance accurately reflects the actual build inputs and outputs.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use platform-provided provenance generators that run outside the tenant's build environment. GitHub Actions: slsa-github-generator uses a reusable workflow that runs in an isolated context. Verify that the provenance builder ID matches the expected platform, not a user-controlled workflow.

slsa_requirements.title: Parameterless Build from Source
slsa_requirements.description: The build should be fully defined by the source repository contents and the build platform configuration, without requiring external runtime parameters that could alter the build output. Parameters that change behavior should be committed to the source repository. This ensures that the source revision fully determines what gets built.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build output is fully determined by source repository contents plus the build platform. External parameters that affect build output are minimized and documented. Any necessary parameters are recorded in the provenance.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Avoid passing build-altering parameters through CI/CD variables unless they are recorded in provenance. Commit build configuration to the source repository. Use environment-specific configuration files in version control rather than runtime parameters. If parameters are necessary, ensure they are captured in provenance.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Dependency Integrity Verification
slsa_requirements.description: Build dependencies must be verified for integrity before use. This includes checking cryptographic hashes of downloaded dependencies against known-good values. Dependency integrity verification prevents dependency substitution attacks where a malicious dependency replaces a legitimate one during the build process.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Dependencies are pinned to specific versions with integrity hashes. The build process verifies dependency hashes before use. Lock files with integrity information are committed to version control.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use package manager lock files with integrity hashes: package-lock.json (npm), yarn.lock, go.sum, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock. Enable strict integrity checking (npm ci, pip install --require-hashes). Fail the build if any dependency hash does not match.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Process Logging and Monitoring
slsa_requirements.description: Build platform operations must produce audit logs that capture build invocations, configuration changes, and access events. These logs support forensic analysis during security incidents and compliance auditing. Logs must be retained for a sufficient period and protected from tampering by build tenants.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build invocations are logged with timestamp, identity, inputs, and outputs. Logs are retained per organizational policy (minimum 90 days recommended). Logs are tamper-evident and not modifiable by build tenants. Anomalous build patterns trigger alerts.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Enable audit logging on your CI/CD platform. GitHub: use audit log API. GitLab: enable audit events. Configure log retention per regulatory requirements. Set up alerts for unusual build patterns (builds from unusual branches, off-hours builds, builds with modified CI config).

slsa_requirements.title: Hardened Build Platform
slsa_requirements.description: The build platform must implement security hardening measures that prevent build tenants from influencing other builds or accessing secrets beyond their authorized scope. Hardened builds run in ephemeral, isolated environments that are destroyed after each build. This prevents cross-build contamination and persistent compromise of build infrastructure.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build environments are ephemeral (created fresh for each build, destroyed after). Builds run in sandboxed environments (containers, VMs). No shared state persists between builds. Secrets are scoped and not accessible across projects.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use ephemeral build runners (GitHub Actions ephemeral runners, GitLab Runners with Docker executor in ephemeral mode). Implement container or VM isolation between builds. Clear all caches between builds or use content-addressable caches. Audit that secrets are properly scoped.

slsa_requirements.title: Non-Falsifiable Provenance
slsa_requirements.description: Provenance must be unforgeable by any build tenant, even a highly privileged one. The build platform's provenance generation mechanism must be isolated from the build environment such that compromised build scripts, workflows, or tenant administrators cannot alter the provenance. This is the strongest provenance integrity guarantee.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance is generated in a context completely isolated from the build tenant. No mechanism exists for tenants to influence provenance content. The provenance signing key is hardware-protected or managed by the platform operator. Provenance accurately reflects the build's actual inputs and builder identity.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use a provenance generator that runs in a separate security domain from the build. GitHub Actions: use slsa-github-generator v2+ which uses reusable workflows with restricted permissions. For self-hosted platforms, implement a separate provenance service that observes builds without being controlled by them.

slsa_requirements.title: Isolated Build Environments
slsa_requirements.description: Each build must run in an isolated environment that prevents cross-contamination between builds. Isolation ensures that a compromised build for one project cannot affect builds for other projects, even on shared infrastructure. This includes network isolation, filesystem isolation, and process isolation between concurrent builds.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Builds run in isolated containers or VMs. Network access from builds is restricted and monitored. Filesystem access is limited to the build's own workspace. No shared mutable state exists between concurrent builds.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use container isolation (Docker, Kata Containers) or VM isolation (Firecracker, gVisor) for each build. Implement network policies to restrict build-time network access. Use separate filesystem mounts per build. Consider using rootless containers for additional isolation.

slsa_requirements.title: Source Integrity Verification
slsa_requirements.description: The build platform must verify the integrity of the source code before building. This includes verifying that the source was not tampered with between the VCS and the build environment. At Level 3, the build platform must fetch source directly from the VCS using authenticated channels, not from user-provided tarballs or pre-cloned repositories.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Source is fetched directly from the VCS by the build platform over authenticated channels (HTTPS, SSH). The fetched revision matches the provenance-recorded revision. No user-provided source archives are used.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Configure the build platform to clone source directly from the VCS using HTTPS or SSH with host key verification. Verify the commit hash after checkout matches the expected revision. Do not accept pre-cloned repositories or user-uploaded source archives. Enable Git commit signature verification where available.

slsa_requirements.title: Build-as-Code
slsa_requirements.description: The entire build process must be defined as code in the source repository. The build platform must use this in-repo definition as the authoritative build instructions. No out-of-band configuration should influence the build output. This ensures that the build process is reviewable, auditable, and subject to the same change management controls as the source code.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build configuration is stored in the source repository. The build platform uses the in-repo configuration for the commit being built. No external configuration overrides the in-repo build definition. Changes to build configuration go through the same review process as source changes.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Store all CI/CD configuration in the repository (.github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml). Disable the ability to override build configuration through UI or API settings. Ensure branch protection rules cover CI/CD configuration files. Use CODEOWNERS to require security team review of build configuration changes.

slsa_requirements.title: Ephemeral Build Environments
slsa_requirements.description: Build environments must be ephemeral -- created fresh for each build and completely destroyed afterward. This eliminates the risk of persistent threats in the build environment that could compromise multiple builds over time. Ephemeral environments also prevent state leakage between builds, such as cached credentials or modified build tools.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build environments are provisioned at build start from a known-good base image. All environment state is destroyed after build completion. No persistent storage is shared across builds. Base images are regularly updated and scanned for vulnerabilities.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use ephemeral CI runners: GitHub Actions hosted runners (ephemeral by default), GitLab shared runners with Docker executor. For self-hosted runners, use auto-scaling groups that terminate instances after each job. Avoid persistent self-hosted runners where possible. If persistent runners are required, implement workspace cleanup and verification between builds.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Secret Management
slsa_requirements.description: Build secrets (API keys, signing keys, deployment credentials) must be managed securely with scoped access, rotation, and audit logging. Secrets must not be exposed in build logs, provenance, or artifacts. At Level 3, secrets should be injected at runtime through secure channels and never stored in source code or build configuration.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Secrets are stored in a dedicated secret management system (not in source code). Secret access is scoped to specific builds or workflows. Secret usage is logged and auditable. Secrets are automatically rotated on a defined schedule. Build logs are scrubbed to prevent secret leakage.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use platform secret management: GitHub Actions encrypted secrets, GitLab CI/CD variables (masked), Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault. Scope secrets to specific environments and workflows. Enable secret scanning (Gitleaks, truffleHog) to detect leaked secrets. Implement log scrubbing for secret values.

slsa_requirements.title: Dependencies with Verified Provenance
slsa_requirements.description: Build dependencies should themselves have SLSA provenance that can be verified before use. This extends the provenance chain beyond the immediate build to encompass the entire dependency tree. While full transitive provenance verification is aspirational, Level 3 requires at least verifying provenance of direct, security-critical dependencies.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Direct dependencies have SLSA provenance available. Provenance of critical dependencies is verified during the build. Dependency provenance verification failures are logged and addressed. A policy exists for handling dependencies without provenance.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use slsa-verifier to verify provenance of dependencies that provide it. Maintain an allow-list of trusted builders/platforms. For npm: check npm provenance attestations. For Python: check PyPI attestations. For containers: verify Sigstore signatures. Establish a policy for dependencies that do not yet provide provenance.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Platform Access Controls
slsa_requirements.description: The build platform must enforce strict access controls that prevent unauthorized modification of build configurations, secrets, and platform settings. Access to build platform administration must require multi-factor authentication and follow the principle of least privilege. Changes to build platform configuration must be audited.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build platform access requires multi-factor authentication. Role-based access control separates admin, developer, and read-only roles. Platform configuration changes are logged with identity. Privileged access is reviewed periodically.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Enable MFA for all CI/CD platform accounts. Use role-based access control (RBAC) to restrict who can modify workflows, secrets, and platform settings. Enable branch protection rules that require PR reviews for CI/CD config changes. Conduct quarterly access reviews. Use OIDC federation instead of long-lived tokens.

slsa_requirements.title: Provenance Published to Transparency Log
slsa_requirements.description: Provenance should be published to a transparency log (such as Sigstore Rekor) that provides an immutable, publicly auditable record. Transparency logs enable third-party verification, detection of equivocation attacks (where different consumers receive different provenance for the same artifact), and long-term provenance availability.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance is submitted to a transparency log at build time. The log entry ID is available to consumers for verification. The transparency log is publicly accessible and independently operated. Provenance can be independently verified against the log entry.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use Sigstore Rekor as the transparency log for provenance. The slsa-github-generator automatically publishes to Rekor. For custom provenance generators, use the Rekor API to upload provenance entries. Consumers can verify entries using rekor-cli or cosign verify-attestation.

slsa_requirements.title: Build Network Isolation
slsa_requirements.description: Build environments should implement network isolation to prevent builds from making unauthorized network connections. Network isolation reduces the risk of builds exfiltrating secrets, downloading unauthorized dependencies, or communicating with command-and-control infrastructure. Allowed network destinations should be explicitly whitelisted.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Build environments have restricted network access. Only explicitly allowed destinations are reachable (package registries, source repositories). Egress traffic is logged and monitored. Unauthorized network connections are blocked and alerted.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Implement network policies using Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, iptables, or cloud VPC security groups. Allow only necessary egress: package registries, source repositories, artifact storage. Block all other outbound traffic. For self-hosted runners, use private VPCs with NAT gateways and explicit egress rules. Monitor DNS queries from build environments.

slsa_requirements.title: Two-Person Review for Build Configuration Changes
slsa_requirements.description: Changes to build configuration (CI/CD pipeline definitions, build scripts) must be reviewed and approved by at least one person other than the author before being merged. This prevents a single compromised or malicious insider from modifying the build process to inject malicious code or bypass security controls.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Branch protection rules require at minimum one approving review for changes affecting build configuration. Reviews must come from a different person than the author. CODEOWNERS rules enforce review requirements for CI/CD configuration files. Review bypass is logged and alerted.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Enable branch protection on the default branch requiring at least one approving review. Configure CODEOWNERS to require security team review for: .github/workflows/*, .gitlab-ci.yml, Makefile, Dockerfile, build scripts. Disable the ability for admins to bypass review requirements in production. Enable signed commits for additional non-repudiation.

slsa_requirements.title: Two-Person Review for All Source Changes
slsa_requirements.description: Every change to the source repository must be reviewed and approved by at least one person other than the author before being merged to the main branch. This is the broadest review requirement and prevents any single individual from unilaterally introducing malicious code or vulnerabilities. This applies to all source changes, not just build configuration.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: All changes to the main/production branch require at least one approving review. No exceptions or bypasses exist. Reviews are conducted by a different person than the author. Direct pushes to the main branch are blocked.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Configure branch protection to require at minimum one approving review for all PRs to the main branch. Block direct pushes to main. Disable admin override of review requirements. Enable status checks that prevent merge without review. Consider requiring two reviewers for security-critical repositories.
slsa_requirements.keywords: two-person review,mandatory review,code review,all changes,insider threat,non-repudiation

slsa_requirements.title: Hermetic Builds
slsa_requirements.description: Builds must be hermetic, meaning all build inputs (dependencies, tools, configuration) are fully declared and fetched in a verifiable manner before the build starts, and no new inputs are fetched during the build. This prevents the build from being influenced by external state that changes between builds and ensures complete reproducibility of the build environment.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: All build inputs are declared and fetched before the build begins. No network access is permitted during the build phase. All external dependencies are pre-fetched and integrity-verified. The build output is fully determined by the declared inputs.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Pre-fetch all dependencies before the build phase. Use multi-stage builds: stage 1 fetches dependencies, stage 2 builds in a network-isolated environment. Use Bazel with --noremote_accept_cached for hermetic builds. In Docker: use multi-stage builds with network=none for the build stage. Pin all tool versions in the build configuration.

slsa_requirements.title: Reproducible Builds
slsa_requirements.description: Builds should be reproducible: given the same source and build configuration, independent builders should produce bit-for-bit identical artifacts. Reproducible builds provide the strongest guarantee that no tampering occurred during the build, as anyone can independently verify the build output. While challenging to achieve, reproducibility is the gold standard for build integrity.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Independent builds from the same source produce identical artifacts (bit-for-bit or semantically equivalent). Build timestamps and non-deterministic elements are eliminated or normalized. At least two independent builds can be compared for verification.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Eliminate sources of non-determinism: timestamps in artifacts, non-deterministic file ordering, locale-dependent sorting, random values. Use SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for timestamp normalization. For containers: use reproducible-containers/repro-get. For Go: builds are reproducible by default. For Debian packages: use reproducible-builds.org guidelines.

slsa_requirements.title: Complete Provenance Chain
slsa_requirements.description: The provenance chain must extend to all transitive dependencies, not just direct dependencies. Every component in the dependency tree should have its own verifiable provenance. This creates a complete chain of custody from the source code of every component to the final artifact, enabling full supply chain verification.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Provenance exists for all transitive dependencies. The provenance chain can be verified from any dependency back to its source. Gaps in the provenance chain are identified and documented. A policy exists for handling dependencies without provenance.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Generate a complete dependency tree with provenance status for each component. Use tools like GUAC (Graph for Understanding Artifact Composition) to map the provenance chain. Prioritize provenance verification for dependencies in the critical path. Establish a migration plan for dependencies that lack provenance.
slsa_requirements.keywords: transitive,complete chain,end-to-end,dependency tree,full provenance,chain of custody

slsa_requirements.title: Multi-Party Approval for Releases
slsa_requirements.description: Release to production must require approval from multiple authorized parties beyond the code review process. This adds a final human gate before artifacts reach production, preventing both automated pipeline compromises and single-point-of-failure human approvals. Release approvals should be recorded in an auditable, tamper-evident log.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Production releases require approval from at least two authorized individuals. Approvals are recorded with identity, timestamp, and justification. The approval process cannot be bypassed by any single individual, including administrators. Release approvals are linked to specific artifact digests.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Implement environment protection rules in GitHub Actions requiring manual approvals for production deployments. Use GitLab's protected environments with approval gates. Implement a release approval workflow that requires sign-off from both the development team and a security/release manager. Record approvals in an immutable audit log.

slsa_requirements.title: Binary Authorization at Deployment
slsa_requirements.description: Deployment infrastructure must enforce binary authorization policies that verify artifact provenance and integrity before allowing deployment. Only artifacts with valid, verified provenance from approved builders should be deployable to production. This provides a runtime enforcement mechanism for supply chain security policies.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Deployment infrastructure enforces provenance verification before deployment. Only artifacts from approved builders with valid provenance are deployable. Policy violations are blocked and alerted. Deployment decisions are logged with the verification result.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use Kubernetes admission controllers with binary authorization: Google Binary Authorization, Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper, or Sigstore Policy Controller. Define policies that require valid SLSA provenance from approved builders. Implement deny-by-default policies that only allow verified artifacts. Alert on policy violations.

slsa_requirements.title: Integrated Security Scanning in Build Pipeline
slsa_requirements.description: The build pipeline must include automated security scanning that runs as part of the build process, not as a separate post-build activity. This includes SAST (static analysis), SCA (software composition analysis), container scanning, and secret detection. Scan results should be included in or linked from the provenance.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: SAST, SCA, and container scanning run as part of every build. Security scan results are available alongside the artifact. Critical/high vulnerability findings block the build (configurable policy). Scan results are linked from the provenance or attestations.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Integrate security scanners into CI/CD: Semgrep or CodeQL for SAST, Trivy or Grype for SCA and container scanning, Gitleaks for secret detection. Generate CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs with cdxgen or syft. Use in-toto attestations to record scan results. Implement quality gates that block builds with critical vulnerabilities.

slsa_requirements.title: Cryptographic Artifact Signing
slsa_requirements.description: All release artifacts must be cryptographically signed before distribution. The signing key must be managed securely, preferably in a hardware security module (HSM) or cloud KMS. Artifact signatures enable consumers to verify authenticity and integrity of the software they receive, forming the last link in the supply chain trust chain.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: All release artifacts (binaries, packages, containers) are signed. Signing keys are stored in HSM or cloud KMS (not on developer workstations). Signature verification instructions are published. Key rotation procedures are documented and tested.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Use Sigstore cosign for container image and artifact signing (recommended for open source). For enterprise: use AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or Google Cloud KMS for signing key management. Sign all distribution artifacts: npm packages (npm provenance), container images (cosign), binaries (GPG or Sigstore), Helm charts (cosign). Publish verification instructions for consumers.

slsa_requirements.title: Supply Chain Incident Response Plan
slsa_requirements.description: Organizations must have a documented incident response plan specific to supply chain compromises. This plan should cover detection of compromised dependencies, notification of affected consumers, artifact revocation procedures, and recovery steps. Supply chain incidents have unique characteristics (wide blast radius, difficult attribution) that require specialized response procedures.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: A supply chain-specific incident response plan exists. The plan covers: detection, containment, notification, remediation, and recovery. Contact procedures for upstream maintainers and downstream consumers are defined. The plan has been tested through tabletop exercises within the last 12 months.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Document procedures for: detecting compromised dependencies (via monitoring services like Socket, Snyk, GitHub Advisories), revoking compromised artifacts (container image deletion, npm unpublish, PyPI yanking), notifying consumers (security advisories, mailing lists), and rebuilding from a known-good state. Conduct supply chain incident tabletop exercises annually.

slsa_requirements.title: Continuous Compliance Monitoring
slsa_requirements.description: Organizations must implement continuous monitoring of their SLSA compliance posture rather than relying solely on periodic assessments. This includes automated checks that verify build platform configuration, provenance generation, and policy enforcement on an ongoing basis. Drift from the expected security posture must be detected and alerted in near-real-time.
slsa_requirements.verification_criteria: Automated compliance checks run at least daily. Drift from expected configuration is detected and alerted. Compliance status is visible on a dashboard. Remediation SLAs are defined for compliance violations. Historical compliance data is retained for audit purposes.
slsa_requirements.build_system_guidance: Implement Scorecard (OpenSSF) checks for repository security posture. Use policy engines (OPA, Kyverno) to enforce build and deployment policies. Set up dashboards (Grafana, GUAC visualizer) showing SLSA compliance across all repositories. Configure alerts for: missing provenance, unsigned artifacts, failed policy checks, configuration drift. Integrate with GRC platforms for compliance reporting.
